policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the place name 'Golan in Bashan', transliterating the qere גּוֹלָ֥ן (gol-an) with its vowel before the final nun. The ketiv גלון would yield a name ordered 'Golon/Gilon', which the ASV does not print. The chapter's only note here (alternative_rendering, 'Or, table-land') concerns the English wording of 'plain' earlier in the verse and does not bear on this unit.
